# Implementation Plan: Core JobTrack Application

**Branch**: `001-core-application` | **Date**: 2026-08-31 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-core-application/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by the `/speckit.plan` command and outlines the design, architecture, and data structure for the core JobTrack application.

## Summary

**Core Feature**: A web-based job application tracking system that enables job seekers to centrally manage their job applications, track application statuses through a defined workflow (Applied → Interview → Offer/Rejected), view a dashboard summarizing their job search progress, and organize company and contact information.

**Technical Approach**: Build a full-stack Next.js application using TypeScript and React. Backend uses Next.js Server Actions for mutations and API routes for complex queries. Database stores user accounts, job applications, companies, and contacts with user-based data isolation. Frontend uses Tailwind CSS for responsive UI with accessibility-first design (WCAG 2.1 AA). Authentication uses session-based auth with secure password hashing.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5+, Next.js 16.3.3 (App Router), React 19.2.8

**Primary Dependencies**: 
- Next.js 16.3.3 (framework, routing, server actions)
- React 19.2.8 (UI components)
- TypeScript 5.x (type safety)
- Tailwind CSS 4.x (styling)
- ESLint 9.x (linting)

**Storage**: NEEDS CLARIFICATION - Database solution not yet chosen. Options: PostgreSQL (production-ready, relational), SQLite (simple, file-based for course project), MongoDB (document-based). This must be decided in Phase 0 research.

**Testing**: Jest (unit tests) + React Testing Library (component tests) + Playwright (integration tests) - standard for Next.js projects, aligned with TypeScript + React stack

**Target Platform**: Web browser (desktop and tablet responsive, mobile-friendly per FR-031), modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

**Project Type**: Single Next.js application with `/app` directory (App Router), `/components` for shared UI components, `/lib` for utility functions

**Performance Goals** (from Success Criteria):
- Page load: under 2 seconds on 3 Mbps connection (SC-033)
- Dashboard updates: under 500ms (SC-034, SC-007)
- Dashboard calculations: under 500ms with 10,000 applications (SC-034)
- List query response: under 200ms for collections under 1,000 items (SC-036)
- Application/company/contact CRUD: under 30 seconds per operation (SC-001, SC-010, SC-011)

**Constraints** (from Success Criteria & Spec):
- Handle up to 10,000 job applications per user without performance degradation (SC-035)
- Zero unauthorized data access (100% user isolation) (SC-019)
- WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance (SC-028, FR-027)
- Keyboard navigation for all interactive elements (SC-026, FR-025)
- 70% minimum test coverage for new code (SC-043, Principle V)
- Zero implicit `any` types in TypeScript (SC-038, FR-030, Principle I)
- Session timeout with redirect to login (SC-022)

**Scale/Scope**: 
- Course project scope with 4 prioritized user stories (P1-P4)
- MVP focuses on job application CRUD and status tracking (P1), dashboard (P2), company/contact management (P3), with authentication as P4
- Realistic for semester-length project with multiple developers
- No external integrations (job boards, email, calendar) in scope
- Initial implementation targets single user per account (no team features)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Violations requiring justification documented in Complexity Tracking.*

| Principle | Requirement | Status | Evidence |
|-----------|-------------|--------|----------|
| **I. Type Safety & Maintainability** | All TypeScript code uses explicit types; no `any` types except documented exceptions | ✅ PASS | FR-030, SC-038 mandate this; technical stack is TypeScript 5+; testing requirement ensures maintainability |
| **II. User Experience & Accessibility** | WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, keyboard navigation, clear labeling | ✅ PASS | FR-025, FR-026, FR-027 directly implement this; SC-026, SC-027, SC-028 verify compliance; design uses semantic HTML + ARIA |
| **III. Security by Default** | Secure auth, no credential exposure, input validation, authorization checks | ✅ PASS | FR-014-021, FR-023-024 mandate secure auth, session management, password hashing, no data exposure; SC-017-025 verify implementation |
| **IV. Component Modularity & Clear Separation** | Next.js App Router structure: `/app` for routes, `/components` for shared UI, `/lib` for utilities | ✅ PASS | FR-032, SC-040, SC-041, SC-042 enforce this structure; feature will use proper directory organization |
| **V. Testing & Documentation** | 70% minimum test coverage; all user story acceptance scenarios have test cases; inline documentation | ✅ PASS | SC-043, SC-044 mandate test coverage and test-driven implementation; architecture requires documentation in quickstart.md |

**Conclusion**: No constitution violations identified. Technical design fully aligns with all 5 core principles. Proceed to Phase 0.

**Structure Decision**: Single Next.js application with App Router provides optimal structure for course project. `/app` directory uses App Router with authentication-protected routes in `(app)` layout group. Public routes in `(auth)` layout group. Shared components in `/components` organized by feature domain. Utilities and hooks in `/lib` with clear type definitions. Tests mirror source structure. Database schema will be defined in Phase 1.
